title: Protocol for Untargeted Lipidomics of Human Serum Using LC-TIMS-PASEF
author: Monteiro, Buzatto

steps.title: Configure LC system
steps.instruction: Install an ACQUITY UPLC CSH C18 column (130 Å, 2.1 × 100 mm, 1.7 µm) on an Agilent 1290 Infinity III UHPLC, set column temperature to 50 °C, and program the gradient as described in Table 1. Set injector draw speed to 60 µL/min, eject speed to 300 µL/min, wait time after draw to 0.5 s, needle height offset to 0.5 mm, and perform a 5 s needle wash for each injection. Run a daily extended wash (30 s needle wash → 60 s 100 % 2‑propanol → 30 s needle wash). Rinse the system weekly with 1:1 methanol/water and then 100 % 2‑propanol at 0.100 mL/min for ~1 h each. Record back‑pressure at 10 % B (0.350 mL/min), 50 % B (0.350 mL/min) and 99 % B (0.280 mL/min) at 50 °C; do not exceed 0.280 mL/min flow at 99 % B or drop column temperature below 50 °C.

steps.title: Prepare internal standards and blanks
steps.instruction: Transfer 5–10 mL of methanol, dichloromethane, water, 0.2 M KCl, mobile phase A (MPA) and mobile phase B (MPB) into clean glass bottles with PTFE‑lined caps; rinse bottles with the same solvent before use. Remove one ampule of SPLASH Lipidomix (Avanti) from –20 °C, vortex 60 s at 20‑24 °C, break the ampule, and aliquot the mixture into amber glass vials with 300 µL PTFE‑lined caps. Store aliquots at –20 °C. Prepare a blank by adding 5 µL water to a micro‑centrifuge tube of the same type as sample tubes.

steps.title: Thaw and randomize serum samples
steps.instruction: Remove ten serum aliquots (5 µL each) and one pooled QC aliquot from –80 °C in the pre‑defined random order; keep samples frozen until use and do not allow them to thaw before the extraction steps.

steps.title: Add internal standard and methanol
steps.instruction: Add 4 µL SPLASH internal standard to each serum sample, QC, and blank using a new, pre‑wetted pipette tip for each transfer. Then add 163 µL methanol to each tube with a new, pre‑wetted tip, close tubes tightly, vortex 30 s, and spin down 5 s in a mini‑centrifuge.

steps.title: Add dichloromethane
steps.instruction: Add 333 µL dichloromethane to each tube using a new, pre‑wetted tip (pre‑wet by dispensing the solvent six times). Vortex 30 s and spin down 5 s.

steps.title: Add potassium chloride solution
steps.instruction: Add 120 µL of 0.2 M KCl (final solvent ratio 8:4:3 dichloromethane/methanol/aqueous) with a new, pre‑wetted tip, then vortex 30 s.

steps.title: Phase separation incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes at 4 °C for 10 min protected from light.

steps.title: Collect lower organic phase
steps.instruction: Using a new, pre‑wetted tip (rinse tip with cold dichloromethane ≥6 times), insert the tip against the inner wall of the tube, slide down through the aqueous layer and protein pellet, and aspirate 300 µL of the lower dichloromethane layer. Transfer immediately to a clean, labeled tube. Perform the transfer quickly to avoid loss; if any aqueous or protein material is taken up, return it to the original tube and re‑centrifuge 5 min at 13 000 × g, 4 °C.

steps.title: Evaporate extracts to dryness
steps.instruction: Dry the organic extracts at 20‑24 °C using either a nitrogen blow‑down evaporator (~15 min) or a vacuum concentrator (30‑45 min). Ensure no liquid remains; cap tubes immediately after drying.

steps.title: Store dried extracts
steps.instruction: Purge the dried extracts with nitrogen, cap tightly, and store at –80 °C protected from light. Dried extracts may be kept for up to 2 weeks, but should be processed as soon as possible.

steps.title: Resuspend dried extracts
steps.instruction: Transfer 25 µL mobile phase B to each dried extract with a new, pre‑wetted tip, vortex 30 s, and spin down ~5 s. Add 25 µL mobile phase A, vortex 30 s, then centrifuge at 13 000 × g, 4 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Transfer to autosampler vials
steps.instruction: Move the resuspended extract to a 2 mL amber screw‑cap autosampler vial containing a disposable 250 µL conical insert; seal with a PTFE/silicone cap. Vortex each vial ~5 s, tap and flick to release any trapped air bubbles.

steps.title: Equilibrate and inject samples
steps.instruction: Keep vials at 4 °C for at least 4 h before analysis; inject between 4 h and 32 h after resuspension to limit degradation. Run the LC‑TIMS‑PASEF method (20 min per injection, including column re‑equilibration).

steps.title: Process raw LC‑MS data
steps.instruction: Import the datasets into Bruker MetaboScape 2025b, perform peak picking, alignment, and initial annotation using MS/MS spectral matching, CCS values and isotope patterns. Apply the custom pipeline for mass matching, annotation filtering, and internal‑standard normalization.

steps.title: Filter and normalize lipid table
steps.instruction: Retain only features passing the desired confidence‑tier filter, normalize intensities to the corresponding SPLASH internal standards, and remove QC and blank injections from downstream hypothesis testing.

steps.title: Perform multivariate statistics
steps.instruction: Autoscale (mean‑center and unit‑variance scale) the filtered matrix. Conduct Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and assess QC clustering; compute PERMANOVA with 1000 permutations (report F and p values). If supervised modeling is desired, run PLS‑DA with 5‑fold cross‑validation, report R² and Q², and evaluate significance with 100 label‑permutation tests.

steps.title: Run volcano analysis
steps.instruction: For each pairwise group comparison, calculate a two‑sided Welch’s t‑test (or Mann‑Whitney U test if non‑parametric). Adjust p‑values across features using the Benjamini‑Hochberg FDR method. Compute fold change as the ratio of group medians. Declare a feature significantly altered when: raw p‑value < 0.05, FDR‑adjusted p‑value < 0.05, and absolute fold change ≥ 1.5 (|log₂FC| ≥ log₂(1.5)). Report raw and adjusted p‑values, fold changes, and indicate increased or decreased abundance.

description: This protocol describes a workflow for untargeted lipidomics of human serum using reversed-phase liquid chromatography coupled with trapped ion mobility spectrometry and parallel accumulation-serial fragmentation (LC–TIMS–PASEF). It is designed for comprehensive profiling of major lipid categories, including glycerophospholipids, glycerolipids, sphingolipids, sterol lipids, and fatty acyls, and supports relative quantification across biological samples. Mass spectrometry–based lipidomics can detect thousands of features across diverse matrices. The chemical diversity of lipids supports their broad functional roles, but also increases the analytical complexity of studying them. In this workflow, the addition of TIMS provides an orthogonal dimension to support lipid annotation through collision cross-section (CCS) measurements, while PASEF acquisition enables efficient MS/MS fragmentation of co-eluting features. The protocol is suitable for discovery lipidomics, biomarker exploration, and comparative studies across biological states. In this workflow, serum samples are collected under controlled conditions, randomized, and processed in batches that include pooled quality control (QC) samples and extraction blanks. Lipid extraction from 5 μL of human serum samples is performed using a modified biphasic liquid-liquid extraction protocol derived from the Folch method, with isotopically labeled internal standards added prior to extraction.1,2 Lipid extracts are resuspended in mobile phases for LC-MS/MS analysis using reversed-phase LC–TIMS–PASEF in positive- and negative-ionization modes. The acquired datasets are processed using Bruker MetaboScape 2025b for peak picking, alignment, and initial annotation based on MS/MS spectral matching, supported by collision cross-sections (CCS) and isotope patterns.
